S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

patient_info.stressor_event: Taking on a mortgage (for home, business)
patient_info.stressor: Cathy’s long-standing tendency to operate best under flexible, stimulating conditions became more impairing after she and her spouse took on a mortgage, adding paperwork, maintenance planning, budget deadlines, and home-related decisions to an already demanding software role. Over 2 years and 2 months, she found that the same patterns appearing at work and home—difficulty sustaining attention through routine tasks, not finishing agreed-upon chores or administrative steps, and disorganized tracking of household and project duties—were no longer easy to offset with technical skill and late-night catch-up. Her visible restlessness in meetings, leaving her seat during long planning sessions, speaking before questions were finished, and impatience during team discussions began to draw feedback from colleagues, though her core job performance remained partly protected by experience. She initiated care herself after recognizing that the mortgage-related responsibilities and workplace expectations were being affected in the same consistent way, and her primary care physician referred her to psychiatry.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: What finally pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up during sprint planning or mortgage calls even when I know I should stay put, like I’ll suddenly need water or decide to check something in the other room.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: I can start reviewing a pull request or reading the mortgage documents with good intentions, but after a few minutes I realize I’m staring at the same section and thinking about five unrelated things.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: If my husband asks me to call the insurance company, upload a form, and then email the confirmation, I usually do the first part and somehow the last step sits unfinished until he reminds me.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: My work tickets, home repair notes, and budget reminders are scattered between Slack, sticky notes, email, and my phone, so I spend more time figuring out what I was supposed to do than actually doing it.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: In meetings I’m almost always bouncing my knee, clicking a pen, or shifting around in my chair, and I don’t notice how much I’m doing it until someone looks over.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Even when I’m sitting calmly on the outside, I feel this pressure inside like I need to move, switch tasks, or do something with my hands before I crawl out of my skin.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: I catch myself answering teammates before they’ve finished explaining the bug or the question, and sometimes I’m already talking when I realize I guessed wrong about where they were going.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Waiting my turn in stand-up or sitting on hold with the bank makes me weirdly irritated, and I’ll keep checking the time or jump in too fast even though I know it comes off as impatient.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I remember teachers in elementary school moving my desk or reminding me to stay seated because I was always popping up, talking before I was called on, or rushing through things even when I understood the work.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: It has started creating friction at work and at home because people have to follow up with me more than they used to, and I worry I’m becoming the unreliable one for planning tasks even though I’m trying hard.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been noticeably harder to manage for about two years, since we took on the mortgage and all the extra paperwork and planning that came with it.
